subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 52 years old, and I'm here because I've been having a lot of pain on the inside of my right elbow. It's been hurting for about four days now, and it's really bad—it's a seven out of ten. It even wakes me up at night, and it's making it hard for me to work on my pottery, which I've been really into lately. Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right elbow, including any activities that aggravate or relieve it? Patient: Sure, I'm 52 years old, and I'm a woman. The pain is on the inside of my right elbow, and it hurts when I try to do things like bend my wrist or use my arm for pottery. It doesn't really get better with anything I've tried, like ice or ibuprofen, and it's been getting me up at night. Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to your right elbow, or do you have a history of repetitive use or occupational strain on that arm? Patient: No, I don't think I've hit my elbow on anything, and I don't have a history of injury there. But I have been doing a lot of pottery lately, which involves using my arm a lot, and I think that's probably what's causing the pain. Doctor: Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or stiffness in the affected elbow? Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hand or fingers? Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or stiffness in my elbow, and I don't have any numbness or tingling in my hand or fingers. It's just the pain on the inside of my elbow that's been really bothering me. Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or repetitive strain to the right elbow, and have you noticed any radiation of pain to your forearm or hand? Patient: No, I don't

Diagnostic discussion:
A 52-year-old female presents with severe right elbow pain (7/10) localized to the medial aspect, worsening at night and with activity, particularly during pottery work involving repetitive wrist bending and pressure. The pain radiates down the arm but does not involve numbness or tingling, and there is no weakness or locking. The patient has no history of elbow injury or prior episodes of elbow pain. The occupational risk factor of repetitive elbow motion in pottery work supports a diagnosis of medial epicondylitis or tendinopathy of the flexor-pronator mass. Ulnar nerve entrapment is also considered due to the medial location of the pain and potential for nerve irritation from repetitive motion. Other differentials such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis are less likely given the absence of joint swelling, systemic symptoms, or prior autoimmune disease. The lack of neurological symptoms makes cervical radiculopathy less likely. No evidence of infection or systemic illness is present.
